newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index closes lower in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index closes lower in slow trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended slightly down in slow trade on Tuesday but analysts expected the index to continue its upward trend in the short term on strong investor confidence in China's economic outlook, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.34 points or 0.20 percent to 169.65 points on turnover of HK$216.7 million, compared with Monday's HK$141.8 million.
The A share index inched up 2.05 points or 0.48 percent to 425.7 points on turnover of 12.4 billion yuan, little changed from Monday's volume.
"What we saw in the afternoon session is just a minor correction," Duan Haojie, a broker with Central-South Securities, said. "The market will continue its upward trend after the correction."
Duan said a widely anticipated new provision on securities-related crime did not dent market sentiment.

China has added provisions on securities-related crimes to its criminal law to help curb insider trading and price manipulation on the financial markets, the Shanghai Securites News reported on Tuesday.
"Talk on the law has been circulating around the market for a month," another broker said. "Investors realise the law is good for the market in the long term."
The law was revised last week by the National People's Congress, or parliament, and will come into effect on October 1 this year, the newspaper said.
"China's markets need to be cleaned up before they can become mature," an analyst with J&A Securities said.
Analysts said the A and B indices have been buoyed by optimism over China's economic outlook, especially in the run-up to the handover of Hong Kong to China on July 1.

"Investors expect the B index to follow A shares up ahead of the Hong Kong handover," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. "Both indices are likely to fluctuate at higher levels in the next two days."
On the B share market, Shenzhen Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base Co Ltd was the biggest loser, down HK$0.13 or 2.64 percent to HK$4.80 on volume of 693,900 shares.
On the A share market, Hunan Zhenghong Feed Co Ltd, which listed 45 million shares on Tuesday, closed at 18.98 yuan compared with an offering price of 7.06 yuan, on volume of 27.0 million shares.
